main_body: Large corrugated-metal roof slope (rows ~47-91) over a brick front wall with arched windows, a central steel double door and copper pipes (rows 92-125), plus a brick chimney
top_band: Roof slope: light grey #97a1a2 rows 49-63 and mid grey #717d83 rows 64-81, then darker #56626b rows 82-90. The roof reads as one wide trapezoidal surface above an orange eave line (rows 92-93) and a separate brick front wall.
evidence: The roof is a wide sloped surface with a flared silhouette and a ridge or vent strip at the back, as in the Beodeul house references. An orange eave line at rows 92-93 and a darker band above it (rows 82-90) mark the front edge and eave shadow. The wall below is a separate brick face with inset arched windows and a recessed door panel. The roof is a large foreshortened top slope and the wall is a distinct vertical south face, so the 3/4 structure holds.

style.evidence: Measured facts: 36 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references, and 9 colours per tile against 18 and 11. Dark edge pixels are 89% neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is a near-black sticker line rather than a tinted material tone. The roof ramp has about 4 grey-blue steps, with simple vertical corrugation lines and sparse rust dots, which is thinner than the per-tile highlights and grain of the references. The windows and brick are decently detailed and flat fills are low at 1%, but the overall ramp depth, outline craft and information density fall below the Beodeul bar.
